events.title: LeNet convolutional networks
events.summary: Yann LeCun applied convolutional [neural network]s to handwritten digit recognition in 1989 — the LeNet architecture that foreshadowed AlexNet.
events.about: LeNet ran on bank check readers for years before GPUs made deep CNNs mainstream. LeCun's work at AT&T Bell Labs proved convnets worked in production — not just theory.

narrative.whyChosen: LeNet was the first widely deployed convolutional [neural network].
narrative.whyImportant: It established CNNs as the architecture for spatial pattern recognition.
narrative.problemSolved: Handwritten character recognition needed shift-invariant feature learning.

sources.title: LeCun et al. — Backpropagation Applied to Handwritten Zip Code Recognition (1989)
